palette.mood: the view from orbit in cold false colour, one warm square, then falling into thawed brown ground and out to a small daylight flame. Different world from the last four films (paper building, dark ground cutaway, pewter beach, walnut desk).
palette.sky: orbital void #0B1020 with grid ticks #1F3A5F; ground-level daylight #BFD6E0 to #F1E6C8 for the final shot only
palette.ground: cold plate (unburned Interior from orbit) #1F3A5F with river cyan #7FD6E0; permafrost ice #9FD8E6; thawed peat #5A3B2A; Fort Yukon spring ground birch green #7BC47F on #8A7A52
palette.hero: SatelliteEye (shelf, kit.tsx, the ONE faced satellite, called the Eye) in pewter-titanium with cyan iris. The three FireSats in shot 3 are episode-local faceless silhouettes (cyan lens, no telemetry light), so exactly one face exists. Throughline: the HOT PIXEL, white-hot core #FFF4C2 into amber #FFB02E with an #FF8A1F rim.
palette.accent: amber thermal #FFB02E / rim #FF8A1F / core #FFF4C2, spent ONLY on the hot pixel, flames and carbon motes (and, in act 3 only, the thaw front at reduced VALUE #C46A2A). Hue about 29 to 37 degrees (rim about 29, body about 37), against 10-22's vermilion at about 5 degrees and 07-23's warning amber, which was a detection-state tint on a cyan scan, not a thermal square.

roles.cold plate #1F3A5F with cyan #7FD6E0: the Interior seen from orbit, rivers in cyan
roles.ice #9FD8E6 and peat #5A3B2A: Act 3 ground only, the only scene drained of warmth
roles.dashed bone #F4F1E8: everything PLANNED (EDF tool, CATG burns, 20 minute goal, empty suppression ring)
roles.plates: ink #0B1020 with bone #F4EEDC text, mono type
roles.hot pixel amber #FFB02E core #FFF4C2 rim: the fire, the decision, and finally the chosen mild flame. Only warm thing in cold frames.
roles.attribution tags: bone #F4F1E8 chips with a cyan #7FD6E0 edge (no kraft, no brass)
roles.accent license per shot: Shot 4: the half-Alaska glow is a low-chroma dull ember ramp #6A4A3A, darker than the pixel and never brighter. Iris and lens lights are cyan or bone. Coins are steel-silver. The SEEING tick is bone. The limb sunrise is a cold cyan rim. Act 3: the only warm item is the thaw front at reduced value #C46A2A.

light.time_of_day: orbital night side for acts 1 to 2, a cold ice-cyan flat scene for act 3, low spring daylight for the last 12 seconds
light.direction: the hot pixel is the only saturated warm light in the cold plate and throws a pulsing ring that tints nearby cyan toward amber; act 3 drains the room to ice cyan and allows exactly ONE warm item, the thaw front at reduced value, which is the film's argument; the final flame lights the ground from a low warm key left

shape_language: a deliberate contrast: hard square pixels, grid lines, the probe, the ruler and the plates (the machine's seeing) against soft organic ground (the world). In act 3 only the probe, ruler and plates are straight: strata boundaries are irregular and noisy, the mat has tussock tops and roots, ice lenses are rounded. Dashed outlines for plans.

casting.hero: SatelliteEye (kit.tsx), called 'the Eye' on screen, the one faced satellite. The three FireSats in shot 3 are faceless.
supporting: IRVision look (reference only, the plate is the film's own OrbitBG)
SmellRings and DashRing as scan and clock rings
Episode-local faceless FireSat silhouettes in shot 3 (cyan lens, no telemetry light) so the accent license holds, built on the shelf SatelliteEye proportions
Spring ground, plan view and burned plain are drawn in the film's own palette because the shelf's RiverBG, TundraBG and DawnForestBG are eye-level side views
casting.net_new: lib/thaw.tsx: ThawProbe (steel rod with depth ticks) and SoilColumn (layered permafrost cutaway with a thaw front parameter), the one small gap the shelf does not cover. No Character rig for Alaska Native subjects. Michelle Mack and Edward Alexander are name plates only.
casting.reason: The story is a view from space that falls to the ground, so the hero is an eye, not a person. The shelf's RiverBG, TundraBG and DawnForestBG are eye-level side views, and shots 6 and 16 are top-down plates, so the braided rivers are drawn on the orbital plate. Shot 15 and 17's ground is drawn as an eye-level spring ground in the film's own palette.
casting.net_new_reason: SoilColumn and ThawProbe vs the shelf: LayeredLand is a torn side-on hillside and CoreColumn a standing banded column with no ruler, no moving thaw front and no burned/unburned state, RadarGroundCutaway is a radar beam over relief, RockGlacierCore a rock-and-ice landform. None takes a foot ruler, a movable thawDepth and a char-top state without a rewrite. ThawProbe differs from DrillBit and CoringTube: it is a thin hand-pushed T-handle rod that STOPS, where they bore. thaw.tsx was registered in the manifest before this gate because make_cut hashes the manifest, which is a mechanical order and not an approval.

motion_language: The Eye drifts and tilts with a slow solar-panel flap and blinks; the hot pixel pulses on a 1.3 s cycle with overshoot when it changes state; the descent is a Stage3D dollyThrough; the probe drops with anticipation, overshoot and a thunk; the clock hand ticks with a spring; flame flickers continuously. 180 degree motion blur on the probe and the plunge.

composition.focal_hierarchy: the hot pixel is always the brightest, warmest, best-finished thing in frame
composition.negative_space: a held, near-empty cold frame at the Mack plate (about 3 s) as the loudest quiet
composition.safe_area: hero action inside y 420 to 1500 for the 1:1; sky and atmosphere above, near plane (reeds, peat, drifting ash) below the caption card
composition.signature_shot: ONE continuous move of about 3.5 s, beats 27 and 28, 65.43 to 68.93 s: the camera falls through the hot square (the shot 8 to shot 9 transition is a morph, not a cut), the pixel-grid cells break up and dissolve into irregular strata, and the two ground cuts resolve under the falling lens before the probes arrive. The probe stop and the burn-scar plunge are supporting beats, framed as a two-up comparison. The final orbit lift is a supporting reveal, not a second signature.

divergence: vs 10-22 (dark spruce ink, brass, vermilion, a bit boring down): this film's ground is navy and cyan, the accent is amber at hue 29 to 37 not vermilion at 5, no brass, no kraft, and the probe is shown as a two-up stop against plunge. vs 10-23 (first-snow white, emerald, plum): no white, no paper. vs 07-23 (beluga from orbit, SatelliteEye, blue-black with detection cyan to amber): that film's hero was a whale seen by the satellite and its palette was a detection tint, this film's orbit plate is a thermal-pixel mosaic and the film falls out of it into soil and ends at ground level.

depth_plan.planes: shots 1, 3, 6, 8, 9, 11, 17 use parallax layers: far plate at 0.6x drift, mid at 1.0x, near particles/ash/haze at 1.5x; the descent in shot 8 adds a haze that rises from 0 to 0.6 across 63.2 to 65.4 s.
depth_plan.flat_shots: shots 2, 5, 7, 14, 16 are locked panels with named layers: 2 (plate under a HUD bezel), 5 (a dark void behind the Eye with floating boxes in front), 7 (arena plate under the scoreboard bezel), 14 (plate behind, roads mid, pixel front), 16 (map behind, dashed unit mid, crew dots front).

accent_enforcement: The per-shot accent license is checked by the pixel critic's colour census and by reading the shot code (only HotPixel, Flame, the carbon motes and the act-3 thaw front use the warm tokens P.hot, P.hotRim, P.hotCore, TH.ember, TH.thawGlow). lib/lighting.tsx AccentRegistry is not wired because Ep1024 owns its tokens locally. The kit.tsx Eye is a named target of the colour census: if its foil or any light renders warm it is overridden locally in Ep1024, not by editing shelf code.
